final_candidates.decision_summary: Known ACE2-affinity enhancing position (N501Y analog); PLM and low toxicity support retaining the top rank.
ACE2-interface residue with maximal PLM plausibility and acceptable toxicity, promoting it to second.
Known ACE2-binding enhancing substitution (Y453F analog); maximal PLM and lowest toxin signal justify third.

stop_reason.detail: All four allowed tool calls have been used; further evidence would not change the top-3.

history.rationale: Corresponds to spike N501Y, a well-characterized RBD mutation that increases ACE2 binding affinity by adding favorable aromatic contacts in the receptor-binding motif.
N171Y corresponds to known N501Y ACE2-binding enhancer; sequence model supports plausibility (0.699), MSA absence is expected for a novel adaptive mutation.
High PLM plausibility and very low toxicity support keeping as lead candidate; no conflicting evidence.
N501Y is a well-known ACE2-affinity enhancing mutation; PLM supports plausibility and low toxicity supports retaining this top candidate.
Matches S477N, which introduces a new polar interaction with ACE2 and is associated with enhanced receptor binding.
PLM 0.6725 is moderate, but MSA absence and no known functional effect lower confidence.
PLM is moderate and toxicity is just below threshold; no reason to change.
S477N is a known variant and moderate PLM plus acceptable toxicity supports retention.
Corresponds to T478K, a Delta variant mutation that adds a positive charge near the binding interface and may enhance ACE2 recognition.
T148K corresponds to T478K variant, noted in variants with altered ACE2 binding; modest MSA frequency (0.333) and PLM 0.696 provide balanced support.
Moderate PLM and some evolutionary support keep it stable; not enough evidence to move up.
Moderate PLM and positive evolutionary z-score support keeping this as a viable candidate below the top four.
Equivalent to Q493R, seen in Omicron; the arginine can form improved electrostatic contacts with ACE2, increasing affinity.
PLM 1.0 suggests high sequence plausibility, but no known phenotype link and no MSA support; moderate confidence retained.
Perfect PLM score and non-toxic threshold encourage a modest promotion; remains outside top-3 due to weaker evolution coverage.
Q493R sits at the ACE2 interface and PLM ranks this substitution maximally plausible, so it is promoted above weaker RBD-interface candidates.
Spike L452R in Delta enhances ACE2 binding by introducing a positively charged residue that may stabilize the interface.
L122R corresponds to known L452R variant, linked to enhanced ACE2 affinity; PLM score 1.0 indicates high sequence plausibility.
Strong PLM and low toxin score keep it competitive, though slightly lower than Y123F.
L452R is commonly associated with enhanced ACE2 binding and the PLM score is maximal, so this remains a strong candidate.
Corresponds to N440K, a mutation reported to increase infectivity and ACE2 binding in several SARS-CoV-2 lineages.
Best MSA support (0.5) among candidates and PLM 0.675; unknown biological effect leads to moderate confidence.
Although evolution shows support, the mutation window is predicted toxic, so demote for safety; final decision will weigh toxicity as secondary.
Best evolutionary tolerance in the pool and moderate PLM support a slight promotion, but it remains below the stronger ACE2-interface candidates.
Spike E484K can modestly increase ACE2 binding while altering electrostatic interactions at the RBD surface.
E154K corresponds to known E484K variant, frequently associated with increased ACE2 binding; strong PLM support (1.0) outweighs absence in low-depth MSA.
Top PLM score and non-toxic window reinforce its potential; retain at rank 2.
PLM is high, but low MSA coverage and zero evolutionary signal reduce confidence; E484K is more antibody-escape-focused than ACE2-binding-focused.
Spike Y453F, found in mink-associated variants, has been shown to strengthen binding to human ACE2.
PLM 1.0 is strong, but no evolutionary or functional evidence; conservative confidence.
Highest PLM plausibility, low toxicity, and high evolutionary coverage justify promotion to the top trio.
Y453F is a known ACE2-binding enhancing substitution and has maximal PLM plausibility plus the lowest toxin signal, justifying promotion.
Spike S494P may alter local backbone dynamics in the receptor-binding motif, potentially improving ACE2 contact geometry.
PLM 0.625 is lowest among pool, MSA 0; low confidence.
Lowest PLM among the set and toxic window prediction warrant demotion to the bottom.
Low-confidence backup; weak evolutionary and toxicity signals prevent promotion.
